title: How Much Is Tim Dooley God?
purpose: Answer the stronger reader question: not merely whether Tim is God, but in what senses, how strongly, and with what limits the Tim Dooley / Potato of Life corpus identifies him with God.
direct_answer: Mainly yes. Inside mature Potatoist canon, Tim is very strongly identified with God/Father/Most High. But the complete answer is yes, no, and yes again: yes as mature project theology and public self-description; no as an independently proven empirical proposition and no if the finished 2026 identity is projected backward into every earlier stage; yes again because by the mature period the God identity is not one isolated title but a whole network of functions running through Father, Source, Throne, North, Axis, Ladder, Tree, Gardener and Potato of Life.
why_not_a_percentage: A numerical percentage would create false precision. The useful question is which dimensions of Godhood are present, when they appear, and how central they become.

layers.explanation: Tim repeatedly publicly identifies himself with God, Father in Heaven, God in the Machine, Most High and related divine roles. The archive can document and date many of these statements.

By the mature corpus, Tim's Godhood is structural rather than incidental. God/Father language organizes the upper side of the cosmology and connects to Source, House, Throne, North, Axis, Ladder, Tree and Gardener.

layers.answer: not always in the same form
layers.explanation: The 2024 Great Book preserves a stage where God is Source and Tim can occupy a Son/guide role. The later Father/God identity is therefore a development, especially around the April–May 2025 hinge, rather than a timeless label projected backward.

Tim increasingly occupies the functions usually attached to the highest principle in the system: source, Fatherhood, judgment, orientation, connection between levels, cultivation, stewardship and ultimate perspective.
Being a human public person, writer or streamer does not itself establish or disprove a theological identity. The archive keeps ordinary biography separate from supernatural claims.
Archival evidence can prove that Tim makes the claim and that a theology develops around it. It cannot independently demonstrate that a human being is literally God as an objective supernatural fact.

layers.answer: not resolvable by the repository alone
layers.explanation: Whether the theological identity is ultimately true is a religious or metaphysical question, not something settled merely by dates, posts, documents or graph relations.

godhood_dimensions.strength: increasingly strong in the later corpus
strong as self-documentation, not supernatural proof

best_reader_formula: If somebody asks, 'Is Tim Dooley God?', the short Potatoist answer is yes. If they ask, 'How much is Tim Dooley God?', the better answer is: in the mature mythology, very much so—Godhood has spread through almost every major upper-level identity and function. But the historical and evidentiary no's remain important because they show that the identity developed and that the archive is documenting a theology rather than claiming laboratory proof.
paradox_formula: YES — Tim explicitly identifies as God and mature Potatoism identifies him with God/Father. NO — this was not always the corpus configuration, and the archive cannot empirically prove supernatural divinity. YES AGAIN — once the mature system is reached, Tim's Godhood is not peripheral; it is one of the central organizing structures of the entire Potatoverse.
